highlights.title: I Saw the Future of Robotics in a Virtual Duck That Chases My Cat
highlights.summary: An OpenAI model helped me teach the Microduck to waddle and moonlight as a tiny cat butler.
body: Allow me to introduce you to the robot cat butler I’m developing with help from AI.

I’m still waiting patiently for a physical Microduck— please hurry up and ship it, guys —but simulated behavior is relatively simple, so it should transfer over to the real thing. I plan to have the robot automatically dispense a treat for my pet bengal, Leona, perhaps by bowing its head to release one from a 3D-printed, head-mounted storage chamber.

I was able to code and train the virtual robot in just a few hours, which is, quite frankly, incredible. Previously, this kind of thing might have taken me weeks to figure out. It was possible because OpenAI’s latest models are remarkably good at understanding and manipulating 3D representations of the physical world and then translating that into useful code, agentic actions, and robot training.

body: Mirra Andreeva won 11 games in a row as she thrashed world number two Aryna Sabalenka to reach the last four at the WTA Finals.
French Open champion Andreeva was 4-1 down in the opening set before producing some superb tennis and taking advantage of an increasingly erratic Sabalenka performance.
The 19-year-old Russian went on to deliver a statement 6-4 6-0 victory over four-time major singles winner Sabalenka.
"I will be honest, I feel like Aryna did not have the best day," Andreeva told Sky Sports.

highlights.title: Queen’s Domain Review: The Perfect Skyrim Replacement for Right Now
highlights.summary: I love Skyrim. I love returning to the spine-tingling haze of ’90s first-person games like Doom, Quake, and Myst. But what I really love is a modern game that feels like a lost relic from that era, not a nostalgic imitation but something that might have actually existed.
body: Queen’s Domain pulls off that illusion spectacularly, embracing the creepy, low-polygon aesthetic of FromSoftware’s King’s Field while building something far more ambitious. Instead of just paying homage to the cult-classic RPG series, it feels like a lost installment, unearthed decades later and somehow better than I could have imagined.

Queen’s Domain requires no prior knowledge of King’s Field, but for those completely in the dark about FromSoft’s history, the studio’s games have never been walks in the park. The danger is real, the stakes feel high, and Queen’s Domain immediately wallops anyone who thinks they have a handle on how to navigate the “easy” creepy-crawlers littering the opening patches of grass. You are truly at level 0 when you wash ashore on the mysterious Isle of Neasied, and the few surviving soldiers you meet early on will be devoured before lending much help.

highlights.title: Supercell CEO believes Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers
highlights.summary: Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen, who last year proclaimed new EU policies risked killing Europe’s games sector, has said newly revealed proposals on the Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers.
body: The European Union has published a draft proposal for the DFA, calling for changes to in-game currencies to more clearly state their value, disclose loot box odds and give users ability to turn off loot boxes - with all IAPs disabled by default for minors.

Supercell has been a champion of the free-to–play mobile space since launching Hay Day and Clash of Clans back in 2012, making billions of dollars in the years since. It’s become one of the region’s most successful gaming companies.
Paananen said while the European Commission promises to protect consumers with new regulations, the opposite will happen.
He claimed that by making it harder for players to buy something, there will be fewer free games on the market. Around 95% of Supercell’s monthly players play for free.

highlights.title: Svitolina stays in WTA Finals hunt after remarkable fightback sees off Muchova
highlights.summary: Ukrainian wins 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 after eight-minute timeout. Andreeva beats Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 to top Group B. Elina Svitolina staged a remarkable comeback to beat Karolina Muchova and remain in the hunt for the WTA Finals title.
body: The Ukrainian looked to be on her way out of Indian Wells when she was a set down and required an eight-minute medical timeout. But she recovered to win 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 and stay in with a chance of reaching the semi-finals.
Svitolina, who was demolished 6-4, 6-0 by Mirra Andreeva in her opening round-robin match, told Sky Sports: “It was not an easy task to do.
“I was pretty angry at myself, after the first match and after the first set also. Things didn’t go my way, so I tried to direct this anger towards the ball and found my game in the end.

“I think the level was back in the third set. I just tried to give it all in this match because I know I would be eliminated if I lost. So I just tried to really release all this energy and find these openings against Karolina. She’s such a tough opponent.

highlights.title: Constantine Director 'Hopeful' for Sequel After DC Studios Shakeup
highlights.summary: The director of Constantine, Francis Lawrence, opened up about the movie's long-awaited sequel now that DC Studios has had a changing of the guard.
body: James Gunn and Peter Safran are out at DC Studios in a sudden and unexpected move that has sparked no end of worry and speculation among fans. Gunn, for his part, cited a distaste for the “corporate” side of the job, but confirmed that projects already in motion, like Man of Tomorrow, are still a-go.

Fans aren’t the only ones scratching their heads about what might happen next. Francis Lawrence, the director of oodles of Hollywood blockbusters, is also in this boat — though he’s rather optimistic about the situation, as it means he might finally get the chance to make another Constantine film.

Speaking with Collider ahead of his next movie, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Lawrence clarified that he isn’t happy for anyone to lose their jobs, but admitted that he’s keen on the possibility of getting Constantine 2 off the ground now that things are changing at DC.

body: The founding team behind Top Drives and F1 Clash developer Hutch has raised $5m to build a new company focused on interactive generative video.
Anorak’s pre-seed round was co-led by Play Ventures and Backed VC, with Supercell and MTG also taking part. Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron is among the angel investors.

The startup is led by CEO Shaun Rutland, who co-founded Hutch before MTG acquired it for $375m in 2020, and chief creative officer Jonathan Alpine, who held the same role at Hutch. David Amor is COO, and cofounder Tak Fung runs the company’s AI lab in Chengdu, China. Anorak now has a team of 20 across London and Chengdu.
As we reported last week, Rutland has been teasing Anorak through his blog, describing it as a studio focused on “interactive generative video”.

highlights.title: ‘How to Rob a Bank’ Review: Nicholas Hoult and Zoë Kravitz Take Their Paychecks in an Annoyingly Flashy, Emotionally Turgid Influencer-Age Heist Movie
highlights.summary: There’s a degree of second-hand embarrassment that comes from watching David Leitch’s Amazon-backed, influencer-age heist movie “How to Rob a Bank.” It’s a film that bids so desperately for cultural relevance, stylistic cool and progressive brownie points that it trips on its own painstaking…
body: From David Leitch, the director of “The Fall Guy,” comes an awkwardly ineffective actioner about a team of revolutionary bank robbers who teach the online masses the tricks of their trade.

Their rapport gives the investigation a buddy-cop vibe that’s meant to be cute and breezy, but Mark Bianculli’s script relies on clunky wisecracks and labored eccentricities that flatten whatever low-bubbling chemistry the actors share. In any case, the intentionally odd pairing of pragmatic cop and stoner chick allows for thematically appropriate banter about the meaning of justice and peacekeeping in a chaotic and corrupt society.

According to the film’s press notes, the four bankrobbers are meant to be thinly drawn, so that the audience can more easily project themselves onto their respective plights: Vince is a war veteran with a young daughter; Hugo, the son of undocumented immigrants; Ryan and Emi, college sweethearts whose baby boy lost his life when a white-collar insurance scam bankrupted the couple, leaving them unable to pay for his treatment.

highlights.title: I went without a car for a month. How much money did I save?
highlights.summary: With gas prices on the rise, the idea of saving money while having a spot of fun was wonderful – so I busted out my ebike for an experiment. This is the best electric bicycle I have ever tested. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I ’m an avid ebiker, especially when the weather allows. During the summer, I drive my car close to 30% less than any other season. I have a few ebikes at home and they all go at least 20mph, so I can get around pretty quickly when I need to. There’s just something about hopping onto a bike instead of climbing into a car. There’s a certain freedom to it – probably similar to riding a motorocycle, but without the extra license, testing and insurance. Also without the speed, but you take the good with the bad.

Also, gas prices are insane these days, so any time I can spend not behind the wheel is a gift. Riding an ebike is a fun diversion from how I usually get around, but I wondered if I could actually do it for a full month and save a little money.

For one month, I rode an ebike or escooter exclusively (with a few notable exceptions we’ll discuss later) and tracked where I went and how far, and used Google Maps to track how long it would have taken to drive. I learned a few lessons along the way – a lot of big pros and cons – from safety to that extra bit of mobility.

highlights.title: A Startup Wants to Fight AI Bioweapons With AI
highlights.summary: Radical Numerics has developed a model that it says can identify natural and AI-engineered pathogens without an internet connection.
body: Frontier AI labs have warned that their technology could help develop dangerous bioweapons.

Now, a startup says it has developed a defense. On Wednesday, Radical Numerics announced that it has developed a new edge model called Omnii Defense that is designed to flag natural and AI-engineered pathogens using a laptop and a USB gene sequencer. It can also run without an internet connection, allowing researchers in the field with spotty connections to use it. Though many scientists say AI-made bioweapons are a low-likelihood threat, Radical Numerics hopes its technology will help researchers and public health officials identify emerging biological threats.

Eric Nguyen, cofounder and CEO of Radical Numerics, says he sees a coming arms race in biodefense similar to what’s playing out in cybersecurity, where threat actors and security defenders are leveraging AI in an attempt to gain an edge.
“We felt that the biosecurity space was far behind on the defense side,” he says.

highlights.title: Monster Hunter Outlanders Review
highlights.summary: This mobile spin-off maintains the gameplay loop and visuals of its console counterparts, with the caveat of how progress gates push microtransactions.
body: My biggest surprise with Outlanders is how uncompromising the scope of its world feels, right in line with a big mainline Monster Hunter, supported by the fact that this game looks absolutely stunning, and runs like a dream. On an iPhone 14 Plus I was able to run the game on High settings with a stable 45fps, and almost zero slowdown, even during intense battles.

The actual act of exploring the world feels just as entrancing as in major Monster Hunters. Various options for constructing camps and equipment as you explore the world make both traversal and item gathering easier. Camps unlock fast travel points and places to rest, catapults send your adventurer flying on their glider at high speed, and resource collectors constantly soak up those valuable items you need.
points: This mobile spin-off maintains the gameplay loop and visuals of its console counterparts, with the caveat of how progress gates push microtransactions.

highlights.title: The Hotel Lobbies Where Hollywood Takes Meetings During AFM
highlights.summary: From the Fairmont Century Plaza to the Chateau Marmont, five L.A. lobbies with better seating, better lighting and a professional to make the drinks.
body: In these liminal spaces, an intro becomes a pitch, and if things go well, the conversation goes on after your calendar says it should end.

During AFM, the Fairmont Century Plaza brings the industry under one roof. But a few familiar Beverly Hills addresses — and a new arrival on Sunset — are worth a trip. Related Stories. Movies China's Film Industry Arrives at AFM on a Domestic High. Movies Can Constantin Survive Its Own Parent Company?

Fairmont Century Plaza 2025 Avenue of the Stars, Los Angeles At AFM headquarters At AFM’s home base, getting to your meeting may involve a few stops to say hello. The Fairmont’s lobby brings together the market’s buyers, sellers and filmmakers over drinks, with the next introduction potentially just one table away. Behind The Bar, glass walls retract onto the patio, letting the conversation move outdoors. The hotel marks its 60th anniversary with “Sip the Century” cocktails, including an Olive Oil Martini and the saffron-honey-spiked Golden State 75. The regular DJ schedule runs Tuesday through Thursday from 6 to 10 p.m.

highlights.title: Grace Cacciato Wins the 2026–2027 S.Pellegrino Young Chef Academy U.S. Regional Final
highlights.summary: Ten chefs. Five hours in the Bon Appétit Test Kitchen. One ticket to Milan. Meet the competitors of the 2026–2027 S.Pellegrino Young Chef Academy U.S. Regional Final.
body: The 10 chefs vying to win the region cooked in the Bon Appétit Test Kitchen in New York City on Monday, and the winner was announced the following evening at the U.S. Regional Final Gala & Awards. Everyone enjoyed the Gala menu, crafted by chef Garrett Brower, the 2024-25 U.S. winner who is the chef de cuisine at Bresca in Washington, D.C. and global mentor chef Aisha Ibrahim.

Representing the Michelin-starred restaurant Saga in New York, Cacciato presented a dish that featured the most components of any in the competition. All the judges were impressed with her sauce work and bold flavors.

Saga executive chef Charlie Mitchell returned for his second year as a mentor, working alongside Cacciato, a repeat competitor. “It was nice to see how her brain works…getting her perspective was inspiring,” he said. Cacciato was equally enthusiastic. “It’s the best competition, and everyone wants to be a part of it,” she said.

highlights.title: Hands on with Home Assistant’s new ‘smart home multi-tool’
highlights.summary: Nabu Casa - the commercial side of the Open Home Foundation, which runs Home Assistant - just launched the Home Assistant Connect Aux-2, a multi-function box designed to help you bring more non-smart devices into your smart home.
body: The Home Assistant Connect Aux-2 helped me track my fridge temperature and finally set up my in-wall speakers.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

I’ve been testing the Aux-2 for a couple days and I’ve found it unsurprisingly useful and surprisingly easy to set up. The Aux-2 is a $69 box about the size of a deck of cards. It has 2.4GHz Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Ethernet, USB-A, USB-C, a digital/analog audio jack, a Grove port for interfacing with peripherals like sensors, buttons, and LEDs, and a pair of RS-232 serial ports.

It can bridge Bluetooth devices into your Home Assistant setup. Its USB port lets you plug in a Nabu Casa Z-Wave or Zigbee antenna in case your Home Assistant hub isn’t in a good spot. You can control devices like TVs, AV receivers, solar inverters, and more via serial connector. And you can connect an amplifier or powered speakers to its audio jack to stream music to older audio equipment.

highlights.title: The AO3 Shutdown Is Pitting Fanfic Readers Against Authors
highlights.summary: “It has left a sour taste in my mouth,” says a Heated Rivalry fanfic author who found her work uploaded to AO3 mirror sites without her consent.
body: Avery has been writing fan fiction for about six years, now mainly focused on the gay hockey romance Heated Rivalry. Until last month, it all lived in one place—Archive of Our Own. Then, on October 29 the fan fiction behemoth went dark due to a “security incident.” Within days, Avery was alarmed to find her works on mirror sites she hadn’t posted them to.
“To me it’s a security risk,” Avery, who did not want her real name used due to fears of backlash on social media, tells WIRED via DM. “One bad actor could put malware in that drive.”
Avery’s problem is one shared with many fanfic authors since the team behind AO3 announced the site will remain offline for up to four weeks.

highlights.title: The 2026 LEGO Star Wars Advent Calendar Is Discounted at Target After Amazon Sells Out
highlights.summary: This year's lineup of LEGO Advent Calendars have started going out of stock ahead of Black Friday. Unsurprisingly, the Star Wars-themed calendar is one of the first to have completely disappeared from major retailers.
body: If you've been hoping to pick up the 2026 version of this calendar, this is probably your last chance to do so at a discount. Here's a quick rundown of where you can still find this set in stock online.

Target isn't the only retailer that still has stock available, but it is by far the best deal you'll find online right now. Both Barnes & Noble and Macy's are great places to check for stock after a LEGO set disappears from all other shelves, but it's pretty rare to find discounts on such sets there. Once Target officially sells out of its own inventory, those are the next best places to shop if you want to avoid paying a mark-up.

This year's LEGO Star Wars Advent Calendar is themed after The Mandalorian and Grogu movie, featuring minifigures of The Mandalorian, Grogu, Moff Gideon, Carson Teva, and a Jawa. Most of these characters are also dressed in festive sweaters. You'll also get to build miniature versions of Mando's N-1 Starfighter, The Razor Crest, a Sandcrawler, and more. The set comes with a total of 293 pieces, which is actually 30 more than what we got with the 2025 edition.

highlights.summary: Russell Brand, who was convicted of rape last week in London, posted on X Wednesday that his Instagram account has been removed by Meta. Brand posted a screenshot reading, “We disabled your account.
body: The British comedian was sentenced Monday to 10 years and six months in prison after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
Brand’s X page, with 10 million followers, is still active. “There never was a Russell Brand, according to @Meta. Thank God for @elonmusk. Stay tuned,” he wrote on X Wednesday.
Brand’s account was taken down because it “violates our policies,” a Meta spokesperson confirmed to TMZ.
After Brand’s comedy and movie appearances tapered off, he started a YouTube channel which during the COVID pandemic became increasingly right-wing and full of conspiracy theories.

highlights.title: Pete Hegseth Is About to Get His Ass Kicked
highlights.summary: House Democrats are already planning to make their impeachment case against the defense secretary as airtight—and appealing to Republicans—as possible.
body: It’s been one week since Election Day, and Pete Hegseth is facing a different kind of war. Trump administration officials tell Inner Loop they knew the defense secretary would face a slew of investigations in the next Congress. Now, they think he is on track to be Democrats’ number one target—and Democrats are already planning to make their case as airtight as possible.
“Hegseth is now a passenger in whatever comes next,” says one source close to President Donald Trump. “And all the outcomes are potentially damaging.”

House Democratic aides tell Inner Loop that Democrats are likely to pursue an impeachment inquiry against Hegseth, and also work to narrow the charges against him to issues that Senate Republicans have also complained about, in an effort to attract their support.

highlights.title: Google’s Tabletop AI experiment lets you build custom collaboration apps
highlights.summary: Google has cooked up a new experimental AI tool called Tabletop that generates customized collaborative hubs to help you coordinate with family, and friends. The Tabletop platform shares some visual similarities with workplace management apps like Asana and Monday, but with a built-in AI feature…
body: “Just add in your links, files and ideas, then prompt @tabletop — or pick a starter template — to generate custom interactive trip itineraries, dinner polls, expense splitters and tournament brackets,” Google Labs design and engineering lead Roman Nurik said in the blog post. “Once your space is ready, drop the invite link in your group chat to let everyone jump in and use it at the same time like a Google Doc.”

Access to the Tabletop beta is rolling out via a waitlist, and currently limited to people over the age of 18 in the US. Some of the example use cases that Nurik provides in his video above would clearly require giving kids or teens access to Tabletop, however, and using this for personal family planning looks like a compelling alternative to stuffy workplace software, so that age requirement might only be in place while Tabletop is in public testing.

highlights.title: US withdraw from U-17 World Cup in Qatar due to safety concerns
highlights.summary: USSF cites state department advisory about Qatar. Competition set to kick off in eight days. The US men’s national team have pulled out of the Fifa U-17 World Cup, which is due to kick off in Qatar in just over a week.
body: “Unfortunately, in light of current circumstances … we are no longer able to participate in the tournament,” US Soccer’s letter to players reads. “The wellbeing of our players and staff will always be our top priority.
“Please accept our deepest appreciation for your commitment to US Soccer and our shared disappointment about these circumstances.”
A US Soccer spokesperson said the federation would not go into details about how it reached its decision. The Guardian understands Fifa was informed of the federation’s decision on Wednesday.

Fifa’s regulations for the U-17 World Cups stipulate that qualified nations must participate in the tournament or be fined, with withdrawal within 30 days of the tournament’s start resulting in a fine of CHF20,000 (about $24,000). Fifa has been approached for comment.

highlights.title: Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra Is Reportedly 'Close to Done,' Though at the Cost of Cutting Back on Content and Length
highlights.summary: Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, Amy Hennig's Captain America/Black Panther game, is reportedly close to being finished, but it could be extremely compromised. According to a new report from Kotaku, Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra is "close to done." The news comes hours after rumors began spread online that…
body: Kotaku's report went on to describe the game's development as difficult, which should come as no surprise to anyone who's been following its journey. The title was announced in 2024 and has been delayed several times, with little to no news or footage beyond that.

Kotaku claims that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra initially began as a Netflix game, but was later expanded for consoles and PC. Unfortunately, the title is reportedly "light on gameplay," with most of the action mapped to one button and the experience lacking "significant interactivity."

The project has also allegedly gone well over budget, and as a result, has had to "significantly" scale back from its original vision in terms of content and length. As of right now, we have no idea when Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra will release, but if it really is nearing the finish line, we could see something next year. Unfortunately, it doesn't seem like the game will be a hyper-engaging action/adventure title with riveting action, from the sound of it.

highlights.title: What is my cat saying? I asked experts to translate
highlights.summary: Slow blinking and trilling are some of the ways felines show affection – but experts say to ‘read the whole cat in context’ I talk to my cat, Blue, constantly. I say things like, “You’re my little baby,” and “Wow, good jump,” and “Can you stop being a jerk for like, two seconds?” She also seems to…
body: She also seems to say a lot, like, “Feed me,” “Feed me right now,” and “Stop working and play with me.”
Because I’m obsessed with her, I like to think we have a perfect, mind-meld level of communication. But what if I’m wrong? What is Blue really trying to tell me? And what am I really telling her?
I turned to cat experts to find out how cats communicate, and how we can better understand them.
First, it’s worth exploring how cats perceive us, as this can shape how they communicate with us. Do they see humans as big, weird, hairless cats? Food dispensers? Or something else?
